notes: Portal home: tidier header and catalog card, “&” instead of “&”

entries.title: Portal home: tidier header and catalog card, “&” instead of “&”
items: A portal with many menu categories no longer squeezes the brand name to “CSL…” or wraps the menu onto ragged lines: when it doesn't fit beside the logo, the menu moves to its own row underneath.
The “In the catalog” card beside the headline keeps long product names inside it (they end in “…”), with the arrows back in place.
Product and category names synced from Propago show “&”, quotes and apostrophes properly instead of “&” — names already stored are fixed when you update.

entries.title: Design your floor plan to scale — by hand or drafted with AI
items: Design floor plan (warehouse page, owners and admins): a full-screen designer with the building drawn to scale in feet. Set its width and depth, and put every zone anywhere at any size — a 4 ft shelving row, a 10 ft pallet rack, a whole bulk floor.

Lay out racking rows in one go: side by side (| | | |) or stacked, with the rack depth, row length and aisle you choose. Reserve zones (SR-10-RES) go back to back with their row; rows that reach the far wall wrap.
Drag to move, size from any edge or corner, or type exact feet. Select several to move, line up, space evenly or match sizes. Undo/redo, zoom, arrow-key nudges.
Add the building itself: columns (repeat across and down to draw the column grid), offices, walls, open areas like staging lanes, and labels.
Dock doors on whichever wall they're cut into — drag them along or onto another wall. Add, rename and remove doors right in the designer; the appointment calendar uses the same list.

Draft with AI: describe the building (“600 × 260 ft, 12 doors on the front, SR-01 to SR-18 front to back, 12 ft aisles…”) or attach a drawing or a photo of a sketch, and the plan is laid out for you to adjust. It only places your own zones; Undo puts back what was there. A new switch, Floor plan drafting, under Settings → Integrations → AI assistant.

The plan on the warehouse page draws your design to scale with a scale bar; zones whose location codes don't split into aisles are drawn as a run of racking with their bays. Plans arranged before open converted, nothing lost.

entries.title: A new AI assistant: Ask Amphora, and a real chat for portal buyers
items: Ask Amphora: one panel on the right for every AI question — a conversation that remembers follow-ups, suggested questions, a typing indicator, and Go there links in the answer. Ask AI on an order, ASN, SKU or count opens it about that record; ⌘K → Ask AI opens it with your question.
Build a report: a new “Describe the report you want” box; after it builds, a summary of what it assumed with Undo.

Portal assistant: a round chat button and a proper chat window in the brand's look (full screen on a phone), greeting the buyer by name, answering with product cards (photo, how many left) and order cards (status, tracking), and remembering follow-ups.

The portal assistant answers anything about a buyer's ordering — and never money or anything internal: prices, costs, invoices and payments are never given to it, it's told to refuse, and an answer that names an amount is replaced with a pointer to the brand's contact.
Knowledge Base → AI in Amphora shows every AI screen, and the related articles show theirs.

entries.title: AI across Amphora: reports in plain words, ask about a record, a portal assistant, import column matching
items: Reports in plain words: on Build a report (or ⌘K → Build a report) type “units shipped per customer last month, top 10” — AI drafts the report, Amphora checks it, and it runs with your permissions. The AI sees field names, never your data.
Ask about this order / ASN / SKU / count: “why isn't this shipping?”, “what's still to come?” — answered from that record's own status, lines, holds, stock and history, with links to where to act.

Portal assistant for buyers: an Ask button in a brand's portal — “what can I order this month?”, “where's my order?” — answered only from that buyer's own catalog, limits and orders, in the brand's look. Off on every portal until you switch it on (Customer → Client portal → Storefront).
Import column matching: when a spreadsheet's headers aren't the template's, AI suggests what each one is; you accept or change it, then the usual check runs.
Settings → Integrations → AI assistant now lists every use with what it sends, each with its own switch. Without a key, everything works as before.

entries.title: ⌘K answers explain how, then take you to the exact card
items: Choosing a Go to answer now shows How to first: the clicks (Settings → General → Picking), what it's for, and the steps from the Knowledge Base. Go there — or Enter — then opens the screen and scrolls to the card, which flashes once.
Fixed: clicking an answer and pressing Enter did nothing; and an answer for the page you were already on looked like it did nothing.
Things set on each customer or SKU say so (“Pricing & limits is set on each SKU”) and ask which one; Back returns to the explanation.
The box no longer draws a second focus frame inside itself, which looked odd in Dark mode.
Settings → General's cards can be linked to directly: totes, offline scanning, license plates, ASN numbering, updates, web address and the license each have their own answer.

entries.title: Putaway, receiving and put-back suggestions are fast in a big building
items: Fixed: in a building with thousands of locations that have weight or size limits, the Putaway page could take minutes to open — long enough to stall a test world entirely (every page then failed). On a 19,000-location building it now opens in a fraction of a second (106 s → 0.23 s).
Receiving's “where should this go” suggestions, the license plate page and Put back speed up the same way (about 0.8 s → 0.03 s per line). The suggestions themselves are exactly the same.

entries.title: Ask how: ⌘K answers “how do I…” in plain words, with optional AI
items: Press ⌘K and ask the way you'd ask a colleague — “how do I give one person a 120-unit limit?”. Go to opens the screen that does it, with the clicks spelled out; Help opens the Knowledge Base section that explains it.
Screens inside a customer or a SKU land inside the one you're on, or the box asks which one.
Questions are understood, not just keywords: filler words dropped, word endings folded, and brand / client / customer (and the like) treated as the same. The Knowledge Base search works the same way.

Ask AI (optional): bring your own Claude, OpenAI or Gemini key under Settings → Integrations → AI assistant. The model list comes live from the provider. Only the question and Amphora's help text are sent — never your data — and answers can only point at real screens.
Only screens you may open, and features this install has, are offered.

entries.title: Ordering limits for each person, per order, with your own message
items: A SKU's ordering limit can now cover Each person: every buyer gets their own allowance (120 each every 30 days), from one rule on the SKU. Leave it on In every group, or pick a group to cover only its members. New buyers are covered the day they're added.
Everyone and A user group still share one allowance between them; they now say so (Everyone, shared · A user group, shared).
Time frame: every N days, or per order — only the order being placed counts. The product shows “Up to 40 per order”.
Message when someone goes over: the brand's own words lead the reason the buyer sees and the approver reads, with the numbers after.
Ordering limits import: set the same rule across a whole catalog from one spreadsheet (Setup → Import, or Import on the customer's Products screen).
Saving a limit now checks it names a group or person of this brand.

entries.title: Saving a user group works again
items: Creating or editing a portal user group said "Invalid input" unless the group was limited to an accounting unit. Groups now save with any accounting unit allowed.

entries.title: A calmer pick queue
items: Each order on the pick queue has one quiet Start (Resume once begun); Fix is the small wrench beside it. No more column of red buttons.
The list's filters sit in two rows: the date chips, then Status, Customer, Zone and Carrier as dropdowns, with Find beside the list's title.
Select all shown is one click; the range box and the slip scanner open under Select by number or scan.
Orders waiting on a kit build are one line at the top; open it for the builds and Open the bench.
Batch these: only the first cart's Start is highlighted, and each cart's order numbers fold under Show the orders.
On a phone the pick queue fits the screen: each row shows the customer, units and ship-by under the order number, with Start beside it.

entries.title: Batch exactly the orders you choose, release a reservation from a location, guided put-backs, bulk checkout counts the whole batch, kit notes, Prime pick faces
items: Select exactly which orders go into a batch on the pick queue: tick rows, Shift-click to tick every row between, Select all shown (whatever the filters leave), type a number range (LUMI-000120 to LUMI-000160, or 120 to 160 inside one customer), or scan the barcode on each pick slip. The bar keeps a running “38 orders selected”.

Batch these builds carts from exactly that selection with the Pick in batches engine — up to twelve a cart, one packing type per cart, the most urgent first, and Keep each customer apart if you tick it. More than a cart's worth comes back as Cart 1 of N, each with Start.
Orders that can't go on a cart are never quietly dropped: being edited, on hold, already on a cart someone is picking, picking started, nothing reserved yet — each is listed with the reason.

Editing an order that's on a cart now takes it off the cart, and the cart carries on. The picker sees “LUMI-000142 was taken off this cart — it's being edited” and chooses Put back (onto the Put back list) or Keep with the order for anything already picked. The other orders keep their bin letters.
Once the edit is finished, the cart's note reads “it was edited by …” instead of “it's being edited”.
When the edit is finished the order is back in the pick queue for a new cart, and its order page shows “Taken off cart BATCH-000042 for an edit”.

Over the API: POST /api/v1/orders/pick-batch batches given orders, numbers or a range; /pick-batch/lookup finds orders by number or range; /orders/{id}/off-cart puts back or keeps an order's picked units.

Bulk checkout now checks stock for the batch as a whole. Before, each recipient was checked on their own, so 400 orders could pass when the shelf only covered 200 and the rest failed partway through. Now each recipient is counted against what the ones before it already need, the shortage is shown by product before anything is placed, and the brand's short-stock setting decides what happens.

Bulk checkout asks the brand's own checkout questions: once for every order in the batch (Order details, beside Ship how), or per recipient from a sheet column with the same name. Required questions are required here too — nothing is placed until each recipient is answered.
In the bulk check, a recipient stopped by a question or by stock now shows the units they asked for (not “0 units · $0.00”), and Fix the address only appears when it's the address that failed.
Renaming a checkout field no longer hides old answers: the field remembers its earlier names, so buyers and staff see orders answered before the rename under the new name.

Every part of a kit now carries a short note on the pick slip, the batch pick slip, the pick station and the pack bench: “Part of kit GIFT-HOST-SET (1 of 3) — also with: SOAP-LAV, CANDLE-01”. If one part is found and another isn't, the team knows exactly what else belongs with it.

The pick slip puts each kit back together above the table (Kits on this order): every part with its stop and location. The same kit twice on one order reads Kit 1 and Kit 2; three of a kit on one line says “1 per kit × 3”.

Short a kit part at the pick station and it says what else to pull: the rest of that kit, with each part's location and whether it's picked yet — leave it on the shelf and record it short, or Fix the stop to put it back. Shorts work as before: only what you record goes back to stock.

At the pack bench, a kit missing a part says which of its other parts to leave out of the box; they stay on the cart for the order's next shipment. The suggested first box already leaves them out, and Put everything left does too.
Kits made in Amphora are now marked exactly like kits that arrive from Propago — on slips, stations and the order page.
The packing slip in the box keeps it brief for the recipient: the kit's name heads its parts, and each reads “Included in Gift Host Set” — no codes, no locations.

Prime locations: mark a pick location Prime and it becomes a fixed home pick face that refills itself — refill when it drops to (min), fill up to (max). Only Prime locations get refill jobs or carry refill rules, and the nightly sizing only makes rules there.

Locations that aren't Prime are never refilled in place: when one runs empty, the SKU's next stock goes wherever putaway suggests, so its location can change as needed. Putaway never offers another SKU's Prime home.

Mark Prime on a location's page, in bulk on Stock → Locations (tick, then Mark Prime — with a Prime filter and column), or with the new prime column of the locations import and export. Watching a location that isn't Prime offers Make it Prime.
Stopping a location being Prime while rules watch it asks first: pause the rules (kept, resume later) or remove them.
Clearer numbers: rules now read “Refill when it drops to (min)” and “Fill up to (max)”, and a refill is proposed when a face reaches its min, not only once it's under it.
Upgrading changes nothing that works today: every location that already had a refill rule is marked Prime.
Pick stops show a Prime chip; Prime is reportable (Stock → Prime location) and on the API (POST /api/v1/bins/prime).

Release from a location: when a shelf is damaged, blocked, being counted, or the product just isn't there, release the order's reservation from that one location — on the order (Lines & allocation → Release from a location) or on the location itself (Reserved here). Choose Release and re-allocate elsewhere (reserved again, earliest expiry first, from other locations — backordered if nothing else covers it) or Release only (backordered). Every release records why and who.

Release everything reserved here: one button on a location re-allocates every order that would pick from it. Tick Keep this location out of allocation and its stock goes on Hold, so no order reserves it and no route sends anyone there until you press Use it again.
Units already picked can't be released — they're on the cart. Lower or remove the line and they become a put-back, as before. Orders someone is picking right now are left alone and listed.

Put back now says where to go: the location each item was picked from when it would still take it, otherwise the best other place (same lot or SKU there, the customer's area, an empty location) — never a location that's being counted or kept out. The list is in walk order, and Print the list gives you the same thing on paper.

Put back with the scanner (Scan → Put back): scan the location, scan the product, confirm how many. Put them somewhere else by scanning that location instead — it's checked against the same rules. Putting back part of it leaves the rest on the list. When the install allows offline scanning, a put-back made without a connection waits on the device and is checked again when it's sent.

entries.title: Required kit choices, kit-only parts, your own checkout fields, a polished storefront, rate card import, phones
items: Kits: a part can now be Required — the buyer must pick exactly one of the required parts in its group (a scent, a shade, a size). The portal asks “Scent — required, pick one” and won't add the kit to the cart until it's chosen; ordering without one, or with two, is refused by name. Required picks don't use up the buyer's-choice picks.

Sold: Only in a kit — for packaging and inserts that make no sense alone (SKU → Pricing & limits). They leave the portal's shop, an order for them on their own is refused, and kits holding them order as before. SKU import has a kit_only column; kit content imports take role required.

Your own checkout fields: in the Design studio (Cart & checkout), add as many questions as a brand needs — short or long text, dropdown, date, number, yes/no — each optional or required, with help text, and for everyone or only some user groups. Answers are checked on the server and saved on the order with its other custom fields; buyers see them on their order.

Import rate cards: one row per card, every fee in dollars, an optional price rise (date, percent, every N months), and the customer codes to put on it. Same name updates the card. From Billing → Rate cards or Setup → Import.
Staff logins are listed under Setup → Import too (Settings → Users → Invite several).
Phones: every screen now fits without sideways scrolling. The top bar keeps search, notices, the knowledge base and Sign out (as an icon); light/dark moved into the ☰ menu.

Portal storefront, polished: refined placeholders for products without photos, a home hero that shows your products, badges only when they mean something, category chips when there are few, a lighter header, quick add on the photo, quieter SKU codes, aligned prices and headings, better empty and loading states — and every page reworked for phones, with Add to cart pinned on product pages.
An import's check no longer sends its rolled-back audit entries to your security log copy (SIEM).

entries.title: Import anything from a spreadsheet
items: Setup → Import: every record you can load from a spreadsheet, in one place — and the same Import button on each record's own screen (Customers, a customer's Products, Categories, Carriers, Accounting, Portal people, Orders, Inbound, Returns, Pick replenish, Settings → Teams).

New imports: customers, shipping accounts, accounting units, categories, kit contents, price breaks, lots (with stop dates), orders, inbound shipments (ASNs), returns, pick-face refill rules, the portal address book, and teams.

Every import is guided the same way: get the template (Excel, with a sheet explaining every column, or CSV), upload it, check, then import. The check runs every row through the real rules and undoes it, so nothing is written until you press Import — and it says exactly how many will be added, updated or skipped, and names every problem by row and column.

Warnings before you finish: columns that will be ignored, the template's example rows left in, and rows with problems — which you confirm will be left out. Download just the rows to fix, with the reason on each.
Orders load through the same checks as one typed in, and an order reference already on file is skipped, so loading the same file twice never places anything twice.
Setup → Import templates is now Setup → Import.
